Data notes for this edition
  • A clean scan. The collector finished at 08:43 ET Friday and every symbol ends on Thursday Oct 29's completed bar on the daily, 4H, 1H and 15m frames; no pre-market stub was found and nothing was patched.
  • The weekly column is a running bar that closes today. The Oct 26–30 bar holds four sessions, so the weekly badges and extensions are provisional until the close; QQQ, MRVL and MU came off up to mixed and ORCL turned down on Thursday's session, and any of this week's weekly changes can reverse today.
  • Deltas are one session. The prior scan is Thursday morning's, which held Wednesday Oct 28's close, so the change chips, the breadth tile and the census all measure Thursday's session.
  • Weekday names. "Thursday" in a card is Oct 29, "Wednesday" Oct 28, "Tuesday" Oct 27, "Monday" Oct 26 and "Friday" Oct 23; today's session, Friday Oct 30, is "today".
  • Volume was ordinary outside the reporters. The median print was 1.03× the 20-day average; GOOGL 5.46×, the heaviest in its 500 loaded bars, AMZN 2.40×, MRVL 2.05×, MSFT 1.95× and IGV 1.50× led, and IONQ 0.60×, TSLA 0.61× and SPCX 0.66× were the lightest. 15-minute volume figures are not used.
  • Nine cards carry a daily chart: MU, AMD, NVDA, MSFT, AAPL, META, GOOGL, MRVL and AVGO. Eight stances changed, every one on its card's own rule: AMD and ORCL to neutral and SKHY to leaning constructive on second closes over their 21-day, SNDK from avoid to cautious on a second close over 1327.62, MU and INTC down to cautious on closes under their lines, AMZN to avoid under its 200-day, MRVL to avoid under 241.64.
  • Firsts and lows, checked against the bars: GOOGL's −12.6% is the largest one-day drop in the 500 bars loaded and its 283.82 the lowest close since Mar 30; MRVL's 218.34 is the lowest since Sep 3 and the largest drop since Jun 5; AMZN's 243.79 is the lowest since Jul 30 and its first close under the 200-day since that date; IGV made its first close under the 21-day since Oct 20; MSFT's 21.73-point range is the widest since Sep 25; QQQ, SMH, XLK, MU, MRVL and AMZN closed back under their 21-day after one session over it; META's 624.52 is its first higher close in six sessions; SPY's 769.36 is the lowest since Oct 26 and holds all three daily averages.
  • Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ by cents. GOOGL's last hourly close reads 283.75 against a 283.82 daily close, AMZN's 244.23 against 243.79, MSFT's 530.43 against 530.14; closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars.
  • AMZN, INTC and SNDK reported after Thursday's close. The scan ends on Thursday's bar, so their cards carry no post-print figure; the headline feed has Amazon and Intel sharply lower before the open, direction only, and all three cards are gap rules from Thursday's bar. GOOGL's and MSFT's post-print bars are complete and their cards are rewritten on them.
  • The daily screenshots show price and volume from the layout; every EMA, RSI, MACD and extension figure in a caption is computed from the scan, not read off the image. The images carry the platform's pre-market quote label; no figure in this report comes from it.
  • Thin histories: SKHY (79 daily bars; no EMA200, no weekly badge), SPCX (97 daily bars; no daily EMA200, no weekly badge), CRWV (no weekly EMA200). SKHY's EMA50 is the scan's 161.51, computed on the loaded bars.
  • The scorecard grades the eight Oct 29 calls on Thursday's hourly bars. MU's and NVDA's shorts were on from the first-hour close after the first hour closed under their lines; TSLA opened over its reclaim with the first target above and was bought at the first-hour close; META and AAPL opened over their first targets and were not entries; AMD, SKHY and ORCL never reached their reclaims; AMZN opened under its floor.

Bottom line

  • Thursday reversed Fed day: 22 of 25 closed down, an average −2.7% on 1.03× volume; GOOGL −12.6% and MRVL −13.2% led on their heaviest volume, and SNDK, MU and CRWV gave back their gaps.
  • The index held its averages, the Nasdaq did not: SPY 769.36, −0.4%, 38 cents over its 21-day; QQQ, SMH and XLK closed back under theirs after one session over.
  • Eight stances moved on the cards' own rules: AMD and ORCL to neutral, SKHY to leaning constructive, SNDK up to cautious; MU and INTC down to cautious, AMZN and MRVL to avoid.
  • Nine of 25 close above their 21-day, from 16, and twelve sit under all three fast averages; AMZN made its first close under the 200-day since July before its print.
  • One of Thursday's eight calls paid: MU's short worked, NVDA's was a partial, TSLA washed, five never triggered; AMZN, INTC and SNDK open on their prints with the feed pointing lower.

Full read: Thursday's session, where it leaves the board, and what the three prints and the weekly close decide

Thursday took back Wednesday's gap in the chips and the megacaps paid for their prints. SPY closed 769.36, −0.4% on 1.06×, at 66% of a 766.62–770.76 range, the lowest close since Oct 26 but over all three daily averages a third day. QQQ closed 715.34, −1.4%, back under its 719.67 EMA10 and its 724.61 EMA21 after one session over; SMH closed 561.67, −1.1% on 0.69×, back under its 565.83 EMA21. Twenty-two of 25 fell, an average −2.7%, on a median 1.03× volume. The largest moves were MRVL −13.2%, GOOGL −12.6%, SNDK −5.3%, CRWV −5.0%, MU −5.0% and AMZN −4.3%; the three gains were META +2.0%, AAPL +1.5% and HOOD +0.2%.

The shape of the day was a morning high sold. Fourteen names printed their high in the 11:30 hour and nine more in the first hour; 16 printed their low in the first hour and then faded, and 17 of 25 closed in the middle third of their range with four in the bottom third (AMZN, CRWV, SNDK, MU). The gaps decided the day trades a third day: AMD, SKHY, AVGO and INTC opened under their holds, META and AAPL opened over their first targets, GOOGL and MRVL opened under every level on their cards, and the two shorts that were on (MU, NVDA) were the only trades that paid.

The board went from leaning up to leaning down on every frame but the weekly. The daily is 3 up, 9 mixed and 13 down from 4, 12 and 9: QQQ, SMH, AMZN, MRVL, INTC, CRWV and SNDK turned down from mixed and IGV came off up. The 4H is 4 up, 9 mixed, 12 down from 3, 16 and 6; the 1H is 7 up, 7 mixed, 11 down from 15, 6 and 4; the 15m is 2 up, 16 mixed, 7 down from 18, 4 and 3.

The averages tell the same story. Nine of 25 close above the daily EMA21 (from 16) and seven above the EMA50 (from 14); 15 of 23 with a 200-day close above it. Five daily histograms are positive (TSLA, ORCL, SKHY, AVGO, MU); IGV's crossed negative and META's narrowed for the first time since its print.

Where the risk sits. GOOGL is the one daily chart beyond −2 ATR at −4.43, with its 4H at −5.22 and its 1H at −4.49, the deepest cells the board has printed this month; META's daily sits at −2.17 and AMZN's 1H at −2.17. The stretched hourly cells from Wednesday have all come in: SKHY's 1H is +1.93 from +4.39, ORCL's +1.35 from +3.96, AMD's +0.73 from +3.34, MU's −0.49 from +3.15. TSLA's daily is the only cell over +1.5 at +1.72. AMZN, INTC and SNDK open on their prints, the weekly bar closes at 16:00 with SPY 13.60 over its 21-week average, and Fear & Greed reads 31.2, fear, from 34.6 at the prior close.

Thursday gapped down in the chips and the two post-print megacaps, bounced into the 11:30 hour and sold the afternoon; 14 of 25 printed their high in that hour and 17 closed in the middle third of their range. The index held its three daily averages by 38 cents while QQQ, SMH and XLK gave theirs back after one session over, nine of 25 close above their 21-day from 16, and twelve sit under all three fast averages. The only trades that paid were the two shorts that were on from the first hour (MU, NVDA); every long either gapped under its hold or over its first target.

Five questions govern the session. Where do AMZN, INTC and SNDK open against 245.79, 93.47 and 1351.76, and does the first hour hold its low. Does SPY hold 768.98 and 768.75, its 21- and 10-day, 38 cents under the close, with 766.62 Thursday's low under them. Does MU hold 929.93–927.24 or lose it for 910.67. Does AAPL make its second close over 344.90 and restore its card one session before the print. And does the weekly bar close with QQQ over 711.59 and SMH over 560.88, or does the week's weekly upgrade in QQQ reverse at 16:00.

Methodology and data notes

Pipeline, rubric, data caveats and sources

Pipeline: TradingView Desktop (CDP) → dedicated "B List Research" layout → up to 500 bars per timeframe per symbol (W / D / 240 / 60 / 15, regular sessions) → indicators computed locally: EMA 10/21/50/200, RSI-14 (Wilder), MACD 12/26/9, ATR-14 (Wilder), 20-bar relative volume, fractal (2-2) swing pivots, 252-day high/low distances, relative strength vs SPY as return differentials. Trend matrix rubric per cell, ±1 for each of six inputs: close vs EMA21, close vs EMA50, EMA21/EMA50 stack, EMA50 five-bar slope, RSI zone (≥55 = +1, ≤45 = −1, else 0) and MACD histogram sign — score ≥+4 Up, ≤−4 Down, else Chop; cells lacking an EMA21 or EMA50 return "—".

Data caveats. Captured Friday Oct 30 2026 at 08:43 ET, before the open; no errors were reported across the 25 symbols and every symbol ends on Thursday Oct 29's completed session on the daily, 4H, 1H and 15m frames. No pre-market stub was found and nothing was patched. The prior scan for every day-over-day comparison (change chips, breadth tile, census) is Thursday morning's, which held Wednesday Oct 28's completed session, so every delta on this page is exactly one session, Thursday's. The weekly column is the running Oct 26–30 bar with four sessions in it: its badges, extensions and RSI are provisional until today's close, and this week's weekly changes (QQQ, MRVL and MU to mixed and ORCL to down on Thursday; XLK, AMD, TSLA and SPY's earlier moves) can reverse on the session. "Thursday" in the cards is Oct 29, "Wednesday" Oct 28, "Tuesday" Oct 27, "Monday" Oct 26 and "Friday" Oct 23; today's session is "today". The 15m column is Thursday's 15:45 ET bar. The final 15m bars carry the usual closing-auction volume spike and those RVOL figures were not used anywhere in this report; 15-minute readings quoted are RSI, extension and EMA position only. The same applies to 1H and 4H relative volume. All relative-volume figures in this report are daily. Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ by cents at the open and the close (auction prints); closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars. Fractal pivot lag. Swing pivots require two bars on each side to confirm, so a level set within the last two bars will not yet appear in the pivot sequence; Tuesday Oct 27's highs have confirmed as pivots in IGV, PLTR and SPCX, and no Wednesday or Thursday level is in any list yet. Wednesday's and Thursday's highs and lows for every name are quoted from the bars, not the pivot lists. "Lowest close since", "highest close since", "largest drop since", "widest range since" and "first close above / under … since" claims were checked against the daily bars with the averages recomputed from them; SKHY's and SPCX's daily EMA50 are the scan's values on their short histories. Every Trigger, Invalidation and level ladder was rewritten on Thursday's close because every card either fired a trigger, gapped past its zone, crossed a tagged level on the close, or changed stance. AMZN, INTC and SNDK reported after Thursday's close; the scan holds no post-print bar and their cards' levels are gap rules from Thursday's bar. GOOGL's and MSFT's post-print bars are complete and their cards are written on them. The daily screenshots inlined in the cards and the market frame show price and volume from the layout; every EMA, RSI, MACD and extension figure quoted in a caption is computed from the scan, not read off the image. The images carry the platform's pre-market quote label; no figure in this report comes from it. Thin histories: SKHY and SPCX have no weekly badge and no daily EMA200; CRWV has no weekly EMA200.

Scorecard. The Oct 29 edition's eight flagged calls, written on Wednesday's close, are graded against Thursday's hourly and daily bars: the hourly bars decide "held an hour" and the daily close decides the invalidation. A short is on from the close of the first hour that closes under its line, including when the open already sat under the line (MU, NVDA); a target that prints inside the entry hour, before that hour closes, does not count for the entry (NVDA's first hour printed 212.08); an open that sits over a card's reclaim with the first target still above it, in a first hour that holds the zone, is bought at the first-hour close (TSLA); an open over the first target is not an entry (META, AAPL); a gap under a hold zone is not an entry until the card's own reclaim prints (AMD, SKHY); a line that is never closed through on an hourly bar is not triggered even when the hour prints through it (ORCL's 137.78); an open under the card's floor and under both short targets sets up neither side (AMZN). A trade that triggers, prints both targets after the entry and closes in its favour is worked (MU, 0.36 ATR); one that prints its first target after the entry and closes back at the entry is a partial (NVDA); one that triggers, reaches no target and closes within about a fifth of an ATR of the entry is a wash (TSLA, 0.18 ATR against). Stance changes follow each card's own stated rule: "held a session" means a second close on the right side of the line, so Thursday's second closes made AMD and ORCL neutral, SKHY leaning constructive and SNDK cautious; a call whose label names a level to keep is graded on that close whatever the Invalidation text says, so MU's close under 951.76 made it cautious; INTC's close under its 10-day, AMZN's under its 200-day floor and MRVL's under 241.64 applied those cards' stated downgrades; AAPL's first close back over its 10-day changes nothing until today's close. The cards that were not calls are not graded, though their Bias lines say what their triggers did (INTC's and SNDK's shorts worked, AVGO's was a partial, CRWV's and IONQ's washed).
